3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I was having a massage and cocktail on the balcony of Palas Toras, high above Monqiz. The sun was setting, its rays shimmering on the water and illuminating the Rumburgian flags flying over the port.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: My masseuse handed me a towel as I got up. Fully adept at blending business with pleasure, I reached for my cocktail and told the attendent I'd be taking the call in the pool.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: As I did, the attendant ran a telephone out to me, setting it on the pool's edge.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: He informed me that Wiktor Smolak was on the other end of the line.

7.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
7.text: "Good evening, Your Majesty. I hope I am not disturbing your regal downtime."

8.speaker: Player_Romus
8.text: "Good evening, Mr. President. To what do I owe the pleasure?"

10.speaker: Player_Romus
10.text: "I wasn't disturbed before. Now I am."

11.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
11.text: "My my. Last I recall, Rizians were a bit more welcoming than that."

12.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
12.text: "So tell me... how are you doing, Your Majesty?"

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "Savoring the high life in one of my many palaces. You know?"

16.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
16.text: "As a matter of fact, I do."

17.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
17.text: "I'm currently partaking in the very same indulgence."

18.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
18.text: "Alright, I will cut to the chase."

19.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
19.text: "Oh, you know how it is. Purging my cabinet of infiltrators, taking out 'personal loans' from the treasury department..."

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: The water suddenly felt cold against my skin.

23.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
23.text: "One you might find to be of interest."

31.speaker: Player_Romus
31.text: "Very well, thank you. A full victory is at hand."

34.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
34.text: "Oh, really? Well, that's good. That's good. Yeah."

35.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
35.text: "A man of few words, are you?"

36.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
36.text: "Here's what I think, if I may be so bold..."

37.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
37.text: "Imagine standing on your palace balcony, watching the sun dip in the west."

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "If I didn't know any better, I'd interpret that as a veiled threat."

41.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
41.text: "Now. Now. No need to be so tense."

43.speaker: Player_Romus
43.text: "What exactly is this glorious army doing?"

45.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
45.text: "...to help you win your war in Pales."

48.speaker: Player_Romus
48.text: "And what do you want in return?"

49.speaker: Player_Romus
49.text: "Thank you for your generosity. Of course we would accept Wehlen's unconditional assistance."

52.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
52.text: "Now hold on a minute... there's nothing unconditional about this."

53.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
53.text: "I'm offering a trade. Zille for Pales."

54.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
54.text: "That's my price. Accept, and Pales will be yours for the taking."

55.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
55.text: "The offer expires the moment I hang up. Thoughts?"

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "Absolutely not. What made you think Rizia can't win without Wehlen?"

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "I'd rather not give up Zille. Perhaps, there's another option we can explore?"

58.speaker: Narrator
58.text: I heard a clink as he put the pipe down. His tone shifted to a much more serious one.

59.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
59.text: "This deal isn't negotiable. It's Zille or nothing."

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "Very well. I agree to your conditions, but only if you follow through with your side of the bargain."

62.speaker: Narrator
62.text: I took a moment to mull over his proposal. Could I really trade Zille for Pales?

63.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
63.text: "So what do you think? Do we have a deal?"

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: I thought about it for another brief moment.

65.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
65.text: "Excellent! And of course, I'll follow through. You have my word."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: I could picture his wide grin in my head.

69.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
69.text: "I wish you a good night, Your Majesty. And good luck in your war."

71.speaker: Player_Romus
71.text: "I hope to never hear your voice again."

76.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
76.text: "Then my people will talk to your people and we will be all set."

77.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
77.text: "You definitely are a man of reason."

78.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
78.text: "I wish you a good evening, Your Majesty."

79.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
79.text: "I'm eager to attend the victory celebrations in Pales, hosted by none other than King Romus himself."

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "They'll surpass your wildest expectations, Mr. President."

82.speaker: Player_Romus
82.text: "Should you betray me, I'll make sure both you and your nation suffer the consequences."

83.speaker: Player_Romus
83.text: "An interesting proposal... But how do I know you won't renege?"

84.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
84.text: "We will sign an agreement, of course! I trust your foreign affairs councilor to make sure everything is airtight."

85.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
85.text: "You're speaking my language, Your Majesty! I look forward to hearing all about all the dirty details!"

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: I muttered the words to no one before submerging myself in the pool.

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: I took a sip from my virgin Romultini -- my mother's invention -- and let out a long sigh.

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: I took a sip from my Romultini -- my mother's invention -- and let out a long sigh.

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: I almost spit out my drink. I took a moment to compose myself before picking up.

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "I was just about to take a leisurely swim in my pool of gold coins. But I suppose your company is a worthy distraction."

98.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
98.text: "'Ha! 'Pool of gold coins...' I'll have to remember that one."

104.speaker: Player_Romus
104.text: "Well, don't keep me in suspense. The anticipation is absolutely killing me!"

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: There was a noticeable pause before he took another drag. I suspected my sarcasm might have missed its mark.

106.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
106.text: "The unmatched glory that is the army of the Republic of Wehlen."

107.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
107.text: "Suddenly, just as its fading light teeters over the horizon, you spot a glimmer of gold amidst the shadows--"

108.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
108.text: "As you're undoubtedly aware, Wehzek troops boast a legendary reputation."

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: On the one hand, accepting Wehlen's aid could tip the scales in our favor, but aligning with the likes of Wikor Smolak could leave us indebted to him indefinitely.

110.speaker: Narrator
110.text: On the other hand, if Smolak's intentions were true, a decisive victory over Pales could be within our grasp.

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: Not to mention, risk tarnishing our reputation with our international partners, especially if we were to lose the war.

112.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
112.text: "I understand the importance of trust and honoring one's commitments -- especially to a soon-to-be brother in arms!"

113.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
113.text: "Just think... this one phone call will inevitably change the course of history. No doubt about it!"

114.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
114.text: "Well, I've had some pretty wild dreams, but I'll trust you on this one!"

115.speaker: Player_Romus
115.text: "A military alliance with Wiktor Smolak... what have I gotten myself into... "

116.speaker: Player_Romus
116.text: "Pales is within my grasp. I can feel it."

117.speaker: Player_Romus
117.text: "I've almost finished what my father started. "The Rizian flag *will* fly over Pales once more."

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: As I set my phone down, I reflected on what just transpired.

120.speaker: Narrator
120.text: I said the words out loud to no one before submerging myself in the pool.

121.speaker: Player_Romus
121.text: "A military alliance with Wiktor Smolak... I can't believe I even considered it."

122.speaker: Player_Romus
122.text: "Pales is within my grasp. I can feel it. Not even a two-bit dictator like Wiktor Smolak will make me think otherwise."

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: As I set my phone down, I reflected on what just transpired.

124.speaker: Player_Romus
124.text: Screw Smolak... I will finish what my father started. The Rizian flag *will* fly over Pales and Zille, once more."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "Screw Smolak... I don't need his help to rectify my father's mistakes. The Rizian flag *will* fly over Pales and Zille, once more."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "Screw Smolak. I don't need his help. The Rizian flag *will* fly over Pales and Zille, once more."

139.speaker: Player_Romus
139.text: "The Rizian flag *will* once again fly over Pales. My father's mistakes will no longer haunt this nation."

140.speaker: Player_Romus
140.text: "The Rizian flag *will* fly over Pales once more."

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: I basked in the serenity, almost able to forget my troubles, when an attendant broke the calm with news of an important phone call, pulling me back to reality.

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: When I reached my private oasis -- surrounded by marble columns with an equally impressive view as before -- I descended the steps and immersed myself in the cool water.

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: I heard him take a puff, likely from a khisha pipe.

144.speaker: Narrator
144.text: With the Pales war a constant source of stress, Lucita had urged me to take some time for myself. For her sake, I agreed.

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: With the Pales war a constant source of stress, Pabel had urged me to take some time for myself. For his sake, I agreed.

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: With the Pales war a constant source of stress, my mother had urged me to take some time for myself. For her sake, I agreed.

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: I was having a massage and cocktail on the balcony of Palas Toras, high above Monqiz. The sun was setting, its rays shimmering on the water and illuminating the Rizian flags flying over the port.

160.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
160.text: "Be glad you're a king and not a poker player. You're bluffing terribly."

161.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
161.text: "Don't be so rude, Your Majesty. I'm asking as a friend."

162.speaker: Player_Romus
162.text: "After everything I went through to get Zille back? Forget it."

166.speaker: Player_Romus
166.text: "I see through your desperation. You're making this offer because you're going to lose the referendum."

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "It's too late for that, Mr. President. Zille is a part of Rizia again."

171.speaker: Player_Romus
171.text: "Listen here, Smolak. Your puny little troops will only interfere with the unstoppable juggernaut that is the Rizian Armed Forces. Consider your offer declined."

172.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
172.text: "The only difference is that this time, our ownership of Zille will be permanent."

173.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
173.text: "But who need dusty old Zille anyway? Not when you've got full control over South Merkopa's largest new natural gas source..."

174.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
174.text: "It's never too late for another agreement, Your Majesty."

181.speaker: Player_Romus
181.text: "Have you opened a newspaper lately? We're closing in on the Palesian capital. We don't need help from you or anyone else."

182.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
182.text: "And here I thought you were doing all that as a token of friendship. Not because of some dusty old piece of land."

183.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
183.text: "Think about it, Your Majesty. Who needs Zille when you have full control over South Merkopa's largest new natural gas source?"

184.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
184.text: "Do you own a crystal ball, Your Majesty? Nothing's decided until the people cast their vote."

185.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
185.text: "Think about it. Lose both the referendum and the war, and you'll have lost two regions. Accept this deal, and you're guaranteed to gain one."

186.speaker: Player_Romus
186.text: "Rizia calling on the Wehzek army for help? It's been done."

189.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
189.text: "It's simple. After we help you win the war, Rizia and Wehlen will sign a land transfer agreement, just like your father did."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "And what if your troops fail? We'll lose two regions in one go."

191.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
191.text: "Don't you worry, Your Majesty. If Pales is lost, our agreement will be void. Zille will be yours."

195.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
195.text: "If you win the referendum. Which is by no means a given."

196.speaker: Player_Romus
196.text: "I'll see you at the Zille return ceremony."

203.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
203.text: "No need to raise your voice, Your Majesty. It was a friendly gesture, nothing more."

205.speaker: Player_Romus
205.text: "Excuse me?! Why is my Romultini glass empty?"

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: My attendant ran to refresh my drink as I submerged myself in the pool.
